title: Trump's Worst of the Worst Immigration Lie: ICE Arrests Harmless Immigrants While 94% of Murderers Go Free
description_short: Trump's Worst of the Worst Immigration Lie: ICE Arrests Harmless Immigrants While 94% of Murderers Go Free
description_medium: In 2025, the administration described immigration enforcement as focused on serious criminals, while reporting showed arrests of people without charges or convictions rising sharply. Reuters found such ICE arrests increased about eightfold between January and June. NBC reported that ICE had arrested 752 of 13,099 people it had identified as undocumented immigrants convicted of homicide, while many detainees had no criminal charge or conviction.
description_long: Throughout 2025, President Trump and his border enforcement apparatus repeatedly claimed to be conducting the most targeted deportation campaign in history, focused on the worst of the worst violent criminals. But government data told a completely different story: Reuters reported in June 2025 that ICE detentions of individuals with no criminal charges or convictions rose by 800% in Trump's first months, from approximately 860 in January to 7,800 by June. NBC News obtained ICE booking data showing that of the 13,099 undocumented immigrants ICE had previously identified as convicted of homicide, only 752 were arrested in Trump's first eight months — a 6% apprehension rate — while almost half of all ICE detainees had no criminal conviction or charge of any kind. Homan continued to repeat the claim that 600,000 criminal illegal aliens were walking the streets — a figure FactCheck.org found to be systematically misleading, including legal immigrants, people charged but not convicted, and individuals who entered the country over 40 years ago. Trump claimed in an April 2025 Time interview that crime rates under Biden went through the roof and were added to by illegal immigrants — directly contradicting FBI data showing violent crime dropped during Biden's presidency; criminologists cited multiple peer-reviewed studies showing immigrants commit crimes at lower rates than native-born citizens.

title: HHS Rescinds ACA Section 1557 LGBTQ Healthcare Protections
description_short: HHS Rescinds ACA Section 1557 LGBTQ Healthcare Protections
description_medium: On May 14, 2025, the Department of Health and Human Services rescinded four guidance documents, including a 2021 interpretation of Section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act. That interpretation applied the law’s health-care nondiscrimination protections to sexual orientation and gender identity. The action withdrew the department’s guidance; it did not repeal Section 1557 itself.
description_long: On May 14, 2025, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services formally rescinded four guidance documents, including the critical 2021 interpretation of Section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act that had extended healthcare nondiscrimination protections to cover sexual orientation and gender identity. The 2021 guidance had been grounded in the Supreme Court's Bostock v. Clayton County ruling, which held that discrimination based on sex encompasses discrimination against LGBTQ+ individuals under Title VII. The rescission meant that HHS would no longer expect healthcare entities receiving federal funding — including hospitals, insurance plans, and medical providers — to extend nondiscrimination protections to patients based on their sexual orientation or gender identity. In February 2025, HHS had already withdrawn its 2022 guidance on gender-affirming care, and the Justice Department had notified the Supreme Court in Skrmetti v. US that the federal government no longer maintained that prohibitions on transgender healthcare violate the Equal Protection Clause — effectively abandoning transgender people as a protected class. The cascading effect was significant: dozens of hospitals paused gender-affirming services citing legal uncertainty. Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, Children's National in Washington D.C., UPMC in Pittsburgh, and Children's Hospital of Los Angeles all scaled back services even where state law permitted them, creating a chilling effect beyond what any individual state ban had achieved.
organization_tags: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services

title: Trump Allies Still Threatened by State Prosecutions - 45 Criminal Cases
description_short: Trump Allies Still Threatened by State Prosecutions - 45 Criminal Cases
description_medium: After Trump’s 2024 election victory halted the federal cases against him, dozens of allies still faced state prosecutions tied to efforts to overturn the 2020 results. The entry identifies 45 people facing proceedings in multiple states, including cases concerning alternate electors. Those cases continued under state authority and could not be ended simply by a presidential decision about federal prosecutions.
description_long: While Donald Trump successfully derailed his federal election subversion indictments by winning the presidency, 45 of his allies still face state criminal prosecutions that he cannot shut down even as president, demonstrating the ongoing legal consequences of his systematic 2020 coup attempt across multiple jurisdictions. The state prosecutions include Trump allies indicted for their roles in the fake elector plot, election interference schemes, and other attempts to overturn the 2020 election results in battleground states like Georgia, Arizona, Michigan, and Wisconsin. Unlike federal cases that Trump can influence through his control of the Justice Department, state prosecutors maintain jurisdiction over crimes committed within their borders and cannot be stopped by presidential power. The continuing prosecutions of Trump allies serve as a reminder that his coup attempt involved dozens of co-conspirators across multiple states, all working to execute various aspects of his systematic plan to remain in power despite losing the election. Many of the cases involve state-level charges for election interference, conspiracy, fraud, and racketeering related to the fake elector scheme and other attempts to pressure state officials into overturning certified election results. The fact that 45 allies still face prosecution while Trump escaped federal consequences through electoral victory demonstrates how his political success shielded him from accountability while leaving his co-conspirators exposed to state-level criminal justice.

title: Government Censorship Executive Order - 'Restoring Free Speech' Through Federal Control
description_short: Government Censorship Executive Order - 'Restoring Free Speech' Through Federal Control
description_medium: On January 20, 2025, Trump signed an executive order titled “Restoring Freedom of Speech and Ending Federal Censorship.” It barred federal officials from actions the order described as unconstitutional pressure on speech platforms and directed the attorney general to investigate alleged censorship by the prior administration. The order’s stated free-speech purpose sat alongside a new federal inquiry into government-platform contacts.
description_long: Donald Trump signed an executive order claiming to 'restore freedom of speech and end federal censorship' while actually expanding government control over online content moderation and directing investigations into the previous administration's communications with social media platforms about misinformation. The January 22, 2025 order prohibited federal officials from conduct that 'would unconstitutionally abridge the free speech of any American citizen' while mandating Attorney General investigations into whether the Biden administration attempted to 'censor citizens.' The order claimed the federal government had 'violated constitutionally protected speech rights' by communicating with social media companies about misinformation, despite Supreme Court rulings affirming the government's right to flag false information to platforms. Disinformation experts warned the order would 'exacerbate the dissemination of false information on social media' by ending government efforts to counter misinformation that 'can pose risks during crises' like public health emergencies or election periods. The executive order represented Trump's broader strategy to eliminate fact-checking and content moderation that had targeted his false claims, using 'free speech' rhetoric to protect the spread of disinformation while actually expanding federal control over online speech through prosecutorial threats. The order aligned with Trump's previous attacks on Section 230 protections and his demands that social media platforms stop fact-checking his content, demonstrating his opposition to both government and private efforts to combat misinformation.

title: COVID Superspreader Timeline - White House Outbreak Cluster
description_short: COVID Superspreader Timeline - White House Outbreak Cluster
description_medium: A Stanford analysis estimated that Trump campaign rallies in 2020 generated more than 30,000 additional COVID-19 cases and 700 deaths. Separately, infections spread through the White House from September 2020 into January 2021, including Trump’s own illness. The figures concern estimated effects of specific gatherings and the documented White House outbreak, not every infection connected to the campaign.
description_long: Donald Trump's COVID-19 superspreader events, including campaign rallies and White House gatherings, directly caused over 30,000 cases and 700 deaths according to Stanford research, while a cluster of infections spread through the White House itself, infecting the president and dozens of staff members. The White House outbreak began in September 2020 and lasted through January 2021, affecting people across the administration while Trump continued holding maskless events despite knowing the dangers. Trump's first major superspreader event was a June 20, 2020 rally in Tulsa where attendees who tested positive included Secret Service agents, staffers, and Herman Cain, who died from COVID on July 30. Subsequent rallies in Minnesota and Pennsylvania saw hundreds attend without masks or social distancing, with both communities experiencing COVID surges afterward. A September 13 rally in Nevada violated state bans on gatherings over 50 people, while a September 17 Wisconsin rally drew thousands with few masks and no distancing, followed by county COVID spikes. The White House security office head Crede Bailey became gravely ill with COVID over Labor Day weekend, with his condition kept secret from the public. By late September, multiple White House residence staff had tested positive, culminating in Trump's own hospitalization in October after the superspreader Rose Garden ceremony for Supreme Court nominee Amy Coney Barrett infected dozens of attendees.

title: Gold Standard Science Manipulation - 'Rigorous Research' Ideological Control
description_short: Gold Standard Science Manipulation - 'Rigorous Research' Ideological Control
description_medium: In May 2025, Trump signed the “Restoring Gold Standard Science” order, directing federal agencies to use new standards for research and the communication of scientific data. The policy placed political appointees in an oversight role and established review procedures that scientists and research advocates warned could limit work at odds with administration priorities. The order changed federal research rules; the implications depend on how agencies applied them.
description_long: Donald Trump signed the 'Restoring Gold Standard Science' executive order that claimed to ensure 'federally funded research is transparent, rigorous, and impactful' while actually implementing ideological control over scientific research through political oversight that prioritizes Trump administration priorities over objective scientific inquiry. The May 23, 2025 order directed the Office of Science and Technology Policy to issue guidance for agencies on implementing 'Gold Standard Science' while establishing new rules for 'use, interpretation and communication of scientific data' that could be used to suppress research conflicting with administration ideology. The systematic manipulation of scientific standards followed Trump's firing of thousands of scientists and researchers while banning words like 'climate change,' 'environmental justice,' and 'biodiversity' from federal research, effectively creating political litmus tests for scientific work. Federal agencies began implementing the 'gold standard' requirements by restricting research topics and methodologies that might produce results contradicting Trump's policy positions, particularly regarding climate science, public health, and environmental protection research. The order represented sophisticated evolution of Trump's anti-science agenda, using rhetoric about research quality and transparency to mask political interference in scientific processes while maintaining appearance of supporting rigorous research. Scientists warned the 'gold standard' implementation created chilling effects where researchers avoided topics or methodologies that might produce politically inconvenient results, effectively corrupting scientific inquiry through administrative pressure rather than explicit censorship.

title: 'Inject Bleach' - Deadly Medical Misinformation
description_short: 'Inject Bleach' - Deadly Medical Misinformation
description_medium: During a televised White House coronavirus briefing on April 23, 2020, Trump asked whether disinfectant could be injected into the body to treat COVID-19 and also raised ultraviolet light as a possible treatment. Medical professionals quickly warned that injecting or ingesting household disinfectants is dangerous. His remarks were not medical guidance, but they were delivered during a public health emergency when viewers were seeking reliable treatment information.
description_long: During a globally televised White House coronavirus briefing on April 23, 2020, Donald Trump suggested that COVID-19 could be treated by injecting disinfectant into the human body, asking: 'And then I see the disinfectant, where it knocks it out in a minute. One minute. And is there a way we can do something like that, by injection inside or almost a cleaning?' He also suggested internal treatment with ultraviolet light, wondering if doctors could bring light 'inside the body.' Trump made these dangerous suggestions while looking directly at Dr. Deborah Birx, who appeared visibly uncomfortable as the president speculated about using household cleaning products as medicine. The comments immediately triggered warnings from poison control centers and medical professionals worldwide, with some reporting increased calls about disinfectant ingestion. Lysol issued an emergency statement warning people not to inject their products. Trump later claimed his comments were 'sarcastic' and directed at reporters, though video clearly showed him addressing medical experts seriously. The bleach injection comments epitomized Trump's pattern of deadly medical misinformation during the pandemic, where his need to appear knowledgeable and his rejection of scientific expertise combined to create genuinely life-threatening public health messaging. The incident became a global embarrassment, with world leaders and health officials forced to warn their citizens not to follow the American president's medical advice.

title: Climate Solutions Destruction - $320 Billion Economic Damage Through Project 2025
description_short: Climate Solutions Destruction - $320 Billion Economic Damage Through Project 2025
description_medium: An Energy Innovation analysis projected that rolling back federal climate measures would raise U.S. emissions by 2.7 billion tons through 2030 and increase household energy costs. It also estimated a $320 billion annual reduction in U.S. GDP and losses of about 1.7 million jobs. These are modeled outcomes of the policy changes examined, not observed results; the estimates depend on the assumptions in the analysis.
description_long: Donald Trump's implementation of Project 2025's climate destruction agenda would increase carbon emissions by 2.7 billion tons by 2030 - equivalent to India's annual emissions - while costing American households $32 billion in higher energy costs and decreasing U.S. GDP by $320 billion per year according to Energy Innovation analysis. The systematic dismantling included undoing clean energy investments from the Inflation Reduction Act, the largest climate solutions bill in history, while supporting Congressional efforts to repeal the law entirely and eliminate over a dozen government offices studying climate change. Project 2025's authors, described as 'climate skeptics,' referred to climate change as the 'perceived threat' while directing elimination of climate research and monitoring capabilities during accelerating environmental crises including mega-fires and catastrophic storms. The policy destruction would result in 1.7 million lost jobs while forcing Americans to pay higher energy costs due to reduced clean energy development and increased reliance on volatile fossil fuel markets. Trump's implementation prevented the United States from meeting international climate commitments while abandoning leadership in the global clean energy economy, effectively ceding technological and economic advantages to China and other nations investing in renewable energy. The climate solutions destruction represented what legal scholars called 'straightforward statement of climate denial' that prioritized short-term fossil fuel industry profits over long-term economic prosperity, energy independence, and planetary survival.

title: DOJ Civil Service Purge - 'Weaponization Working Group' Retaliation
description_short: DOJ Civil Service Purge - 'Weaponization Working Group' Retaliation
description_medium: The Justice Department dismissed at least 35 employees who had worked on Special Counsel Jack Smith’s investigations or January 6 cases, according to the supplied account. The department also created a “weaponization working group” to review past investigations and identify personnel for possible discipline. The dismissals and review raised questions about protections for career staff and whether investigative work would be treated as grounds for retaliation.
description_long: Donald Trump's Justice Department systematically purged career prosecutors, FBI agents, and DOJ staff who had investigated January 6th or prosecuted Trump's cases, firing at least 35 employees from Special Counsel Jack Smith's teams while creating a 'weaponization working group' to identify and terminate anyone who had opposed him. Attorney General Pam Bondi fired the department's top ethics chief and approximately 20 other DOJ employees in a weekend purge, while directing the creation of hit lists targeting prosecutors and FBI agents who had 'significant roles in prosecuting the President.' The administration fired four career officials in the Executive Office of Immigration Review on January 20, including the Chief Immigration Judge, followed by systematic targeting of anyone connected to Trump's criminal cases. Acting Deputy Attorney General Emil Bove ordered federal prosecutors to compile lists of all prosecutors and FBI agents who worked on January 6th investigations, titling the memo 'Terminations' to make clear the intent. The purge violated federal civil service laws protecting career employees from partisan retaliation, with the FBI Agents Association filing lawsuits alleging First Amendment and Due Process violations. Mass resignations and firings left the DOJ's voting rights section with only three attorneys and the Federal Programs Branch with two-thirds of its staff gone, crippling essential government functions while eliminating anyone who might hold Trump accountable for future misconduct.

title: Dark Money Record - $1.9 Billion in Secret Election Funding
description_short: Dark Money Record - $1.9 Billion in Secret Election Funding
description_medium: Dark-money groups spent a record $1.9 billion in the 2024 election cycle, with some spending supporting Trump while obscuring the identities of donors. The Brennan Center’s account names groups including Securing American Greatness and Building America’s Future. The spending illustrates how outside organizations can shape federal elections while disclosure rules leave voters unable to identify all major funders.
description_long: The 2024 election saw a record-breaking $1.9 billion in dark money spending - funds from undisclosed donors that cannot be traced to their sources - with multiple secretive groups supporting Donald Trump's campaign while obscuring the identities of wealthy donors seeking to influence American politics. Trump-supporting dark money groups included Securing American Greatness, which spent over $81 million after incorporation in March 2024, and Building America's Future, reportedly funded by Elon Musk, which contributed over $35 million to super PACs. The Brennan Center found that political committees supporting Trump or Harris collectively received more than $500 million from dark money groups, with spending by undisclosed donors becoming increasingly difficult to trace. Trump's dark money network operated alongside traditional super PACs, with groups like Securing American Greatness run by Trump ally Taylor Budowich, who also oversaw the principal pro-Trump super PAC MAGA Inc. The unprecedented scale of secret funding allowed billionaires and foreign interests to potentially influence American elections without public knowledge, undermining democratic transparency and accountability. Some dark money groups supporting Trump used deceptive tactics, with Building America's Future creating fake pro-Harris ads that actually promoted divisive policies to damage her campaign. The $1.9 billion in dark money represented a massive increase from previous cycles, showing how wealthy interests increasingly used untraceable funding to shape American politics while avoiding public scrutiny.

title: Bitcoin Strategic Reserve Executive Order: Government Endorses Presidential Asset
description_short: Bitcoin Strategic Reserve Executive Order: Government Endorses Presidential Asset
description_medium: On March 6, 2025, Trump signed an executive order establishing a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve within the Treasury Department. It directs agencies to transfer bitcoin seized through criminal or civil forfeiture into the reserve and creates a separate stockpile for other digital assets. The order also bars the sale of bitcoin held in the reserve, turning previously forfeited assets into a federal holding.
description_long: On March 6, 2025, President Trump signed Executive Order 14233 establishing the U.S. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve, directing all federal agencies to transfer Bitcoin seized through criminal and civil forfeitures to a Treasury Department reserve. The order also created a separate Digital Asset Stockpile for non-Bitcoin cryptocurrencies and prohibited the sale of any Bitcoin in the reserve. Trump's crypto czar David Sacks announced the government held approximately 200,000 Bitcoin worth roughly $17 billion at the time; later estimates ranged as high as 328,372 BTC worth approximately $21 billion by mid-2026. The order directed Treasury and Commerce to develop budget-neutral strategies to acquire additional Bitcoin. The executive order came amid Trump family ownership of massive Bitcoin-adjacent financial interests through the $TRUMP memecoin and World Liberty Financial, meaning a rising Bitcoin market — boosted by government legitimization — would directly enrich the Trump family. Critics noted that Trump's own financial disclosures showed over $1.4 billion in crypto income in 2025, making him the first U.S. president to issue major crypto policy while holding enormous personal crypto stakes. title: Silicon Valley Capitulates: Zuckerberg Ends Fact-Checking, Musk Amplifies Trump Disinformation on X
description_short: Silicon Valley Capitulates: Zuckerberg Ends Fact-Checking, Musk Amplifies Trump Disinformation on X
description_medium: On January 7, 2025, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced that the company would end its U.S. third-party fact-checking program on Facebook, Instagram, and Threads and adopt a Community Notes model similar to X’s. He cited concerns about mistakes and censorship, and the announcement came with other policy changes ahead of Trump’s inauguration. The shift affected content moderation across platforms used by billions of people.
description_long: On January 7, 2025 — less than two weeks before Trump's inauguration — Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced the elimination of Meta's third-party fact-checking program across Facebook, Instagram, and Threads, affecting more than 3 billion users, replacing it with an X-style Community Notes model and explicitly citing Elon Musk's approach as inspiration; Zuckerberg declared we've reached a point where it's just too many mistakes and too much censorship and donated $1 million to Trump's inaugural fund. Meta moved its trust and safety teams from California to Texas, elevated longtime Republican insider Joel Kaplan to head of global policy, removed special restrictions on Trump's accounts imposed after January 6, and dropped content limits on immigration and gender identity discussions — moves Bloomberg described as aimed at an audience of one as Zuckerberg sought to mend fences with the incoming administration. Musk, having acquired Twitter/X in 2022 for $44 billion, had already dismantled most of the platform's content moderation infrastructure and reinstated thousands of suspended far-right accounts; in 2025, X became the primary platform for White House messaging while Musk served in the administration. The simultaneous capitulations of Meta and X — the two largest social media platforms in the world — removed institutional misinformation safeguards covering the majority of Americans' online news consumption just as the Trump administration began its second term.

title: Keeping Men Out of Women's Sports EO Bans Trans Athletes
description_short: Keeping Men Out of Women's Sports EO Bans Trans Athletes
description_medium: On February 5, 2025, Trump signed an executive order directing federal agencies to bar transgender girls and women from female-designated school sports under the administration’s interpretation of Title IX. It also threatened to withhold federal funding from schools that allowed them to compete. The order instructed the Education Department and Justice Department to enforce the policy, placing federal grants at the center of the dispute.
description_long: On February 5, 2025 — coinciding with National Girls and Women in Sports Day — Trump signed the executive order Keeping Men Out of Women's Sports, directing federal agencies to enforce a ban on transgender women and girls competing in female-designated school sports under a reinterpreted Title IX. The order threatened to cut off all federal funding to any school allowing transgender women or girls to compete in female sports. Despite the sweeping framing, the NCAA president had testified before Congress in December 2024 that he was aware of fewer than 10 transgender athletes among the 530,000 competing at 1,100 member schools — making the executive action an enormous policy hammer targeting a vanishingly small population. The order directed the Department of Justice to ensure all government agencies enforce the sports ban and instructed the Department of Education to change its Title IX enforcement interpretation accordingly. The following day, the Education Department opened a Title IX investigation into the University of Pennsylvania over swimmer Lia Thomas, who had competed for Penn and won the 2022 NCAA championship in the women's 500-yard freestyle — three years before the order was signed. Scores of state-level sports bans were already in effect across Republican-controlled states, meaning the federal order functioned primarily as a funding coercion tool against the remaining schools that had maintained inclusive policies.

title: Decorated Trans Troops Forcibly Discharged; Denied Uniforms at Retirement
description_short: Decorated Trans Troops Forcibly Discharged; Denied Uniforms at Retirement
description_medium: By 2025, transgender service members were being separated from the military under the administration’s policy. More than 1,000 had entered the separation process by May, including decorated personnel with long records of service. Veterans described losing access to retirement benefits, health coverage, or the ability to leave in uniform. The account follows several named service members and the effects of the policy on their careers.
description_long: By summer 2025, thousands of transgender service members were being separated from the U.S. military in a process multiple veterans described as open cruelty and dehumanizing. Among those forced out: Navy Commander Emily Shilling, 42, who had flown over 60 combat missions in Iraq and Afghanistan and served nearly two decades; Air Force Master Sgt. Logan Ireland, a decorated veteran stationed at Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam, Hawaii, who initially qualified for an early retirement program only to be told on August 4 that transgender troops with 15-18 years of service no longer qualified; Army Staff Sgt. Allison Ravelli, a combat medic at Fort Rucker, Alabama, whose 3-year-old daughter was set to lose Tricare health benefits; and Navy Medical Service Corps officer Sam Rodriguez, 38, who had their officer training school orders canceled days after the Supreme Court decision. The Pentagon reversed gender markers in service records, stripping many transgender troops of the right to wear the uniform they had served in. Transgender officers were assigned discharge code JDK, labeling them a national security threat. Air Force Technical Sgt. Rylee Marcotte was denied her uniform for her final outprocessing appointment. Space Force Col. Bree Fram, an astronautical engineer and leader among trans service members who had served for decades, could not retire in uniform. Over 1,000 had entered the separation pipeline by May 2025.

title: ICE Arrests Journalists Covering Immigration — Spanish-Language Reporter Estefany Rodriguez Detained 16 Days
description_short: ICE Arrests Journalists Covering Immigration — Spanish-Language Reporter Estefany Rodriguez Detained 16 Days
description_medium: On March 4, 2026, ICE detained Nashville Noticias reporter Estefany Rodriguez Florez after agents surrounded the marked press vehicle she was using. Her attorneys called the arrest retaliatory, and she remained in immigration custody for more than 16 days before her release on bond on March 20. Press-freedom groups cited the case amid other arrests and searches involving journalists covering immigration and protests.
description_long: On March 4, 2026, ICE agents surrounded the marked Nashville Noticias press vehicle carrying Estefany Rodriguez Florez — a Colombian-born journalist who had fled death threats for her crime coverage in Bogota — and detained her without presenting a judicial warrant, in what her attorneys called a retaliatory arrest targeting a reporter frequently critical of ICE. Rodriguez was held in ICE custody for over 16 days, transferred to Etowah County Jail in Alabama and then to the South Louisiana ICE Processing Center in Basile, Louisiana, before a judge finally allowed bond; she was released March 20, 2026. The Committee to Protect Journalists documented at least two similar cases: journalist Mario Guevara was detained near Atlanta and ultimately deported, having fled El Salvador after receiving death threats. The CPJ also documented the October 2025 arrest of British political commentator Sami Hamdi at San Francisco International Airport after his visa was revoked without notification, and in January 2026, FBI agents raided the Virginia home of Washington Post reporter Hannah Natanson and seized her electronic devices and work laptop in a leak investigation. Press freedom groups noted that ICE also arrested independent journalist Georgia Fort in January 2026 while she was covering a Minnesota church protest against immigration enforcement, with journalists Don Lemon, Junn Bollmann, and Michael Walker Beute facing similar federal charges from the same event.

title: State Electoral Pressure Campaign - 'Find 11,780 Votes' Criminal Scheme
description_short: State Electoral Pressure Campaign - 'Find 11,780 Votes' Criminal Scheme
description_medium: On January 2, 2021, Trump called Georgia Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger and urged him to “find 11,780 votes,” the margin needed to reverse Joe Biden’s victory in Georgia. Trump also pressed other state officials to challenge certified results. The call became a central part of investigations into efforts to overturn the 2020 election and showed the pressure placed on officials administering it.
description_long: Donald Trump conducted an unprecedented pressure campaign against state election officials to overturn legitimate election results, culminating in his January 2, 2021 phone call demanding Georgia Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger 'find 11,780 votes' to reverse his loss - the exact number needed to overturn Joe Biden's victory. Trump's state-level coup attempt included calling Georgia Governor Brian Kemp to demand a special legislative session to override election results, contacting Pennsylvania's House speaker with similar objectives, and inviting Michigan Republican officials to the White House to discuss changing their state's results. The pressure campaign violated both state and federal laws against election interference, with Trump threatening criminal prosecution of officials who refused to cooperate and suggesting they were committing crimes by certifying legitimate results. In the notorious Georgia call, Trump made false claims about dead voters, ballot shredding, and vote switching while pressuring Raffensperger to 'find' votes that didn't exist, warning the secretary of state faced 'a big risk' for not helping. Trump also called the chief investigator in Georgia's Secretary of State office, urging him to 'find the fraud' in mail ballot investigations that ultimately found no evidence of wrongdoing. The systematic targeting of state officials represented an unprecedented federal interference in state election administration, with Trump using the weight of the presidency to coerce officials into overturning certified results through threats and intimidation.

title: Admin Defies Court Order, Illegally Deports Kilmar Abrego Garcia
description_short: Admin Defies Court Order, Illegally Deports Kilmar Abrego Garcia
description_medium: In March 2025, federal officials deported Kilmar Abrego Garcia to El Salvador despite a 2019 immigration order barring his removal there. The government acknowledged the deportation was an administrative error. The Supreme Court later ruled unanimously that the administration had to facilitate his return to the United States, turning the case into a test of compliance with a court order.
description_long: On March 12, 2025, DHS agents arrested Kilmar Abrego Garcia — a Maryland father of three with no criminal record — during a routine traffic stop, giving his wife ten minutes to collect their five-year-old child with disabilities before handing the boy to Child Protective Services. Three days later, despite a 2019 immigration judge's withholding order specifically barring his removal to El Salvador, Abrego Garcia was flown to CECOT, El Salvador's notorious terrorism mega-prison. The government acknowledged the removal was an administrative error. Federal courts ordered his return. On April 10, 2025, the Supreme Court ruled 9-0 that the administration must facilitate his return to the United States, affirming the deportation was illegal. The administration refused to comply in good faith, with DHS filing a declaration claiming it had no authority to secure his return. In an Oval Office meeting, Trump hosted Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele, who publicly refused to return Abrego Garcia. Trump then made a veiled threat, commenting to Bukele: Homegrown criminals next. Justice Sotomayor warned in a concurrence that the government's position implied it could deport and imprison any person — including U.S. citizens — without legal consequence. As of December 2025, Abrego Garcia had been returned to the U.S. but a federal judge was still blocking his re-detainment, saying she did not trust the administration not to illegally deport him again.

title: Nepotism Empire - Ivanka and Jared's $640 Million White House Windfall
description_short: Nepotism Empire - Ivanka and Jared's $640 Million White House Windfall
description_medium: While serving as White House advisers, Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner reported outside income ranging from $172 million to $640 million over four years, according to Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington. Their portfolios included major policy areas while they retained private business interests. Ivanka also received foreign trademark approvals, including in China, raising questions about the overlap between public office and family business.
description_long: While serving as unpaid White House advisors to avoid anti-nepotism laws, Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner made between $172 million and $640 million in outside income during their four years in the Trump administration, according to Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington. Despite having no relevant qualifications, Trump appointed his daughter and son-in-law to senior advisor positions with sweeping portfolios including Middle East peace, criminal justice reform, and economic policy. The couple's appointment violated the spirit and intent of federal anti-nepotism statutes, which were created after JFK appointed his brother as Attorney General. While they waived government salaries, they continued profiting from business interests that created massive conflicts of interest. Ivanka Trump received over 28 foreign trademarks, including 16 from China, often after beneficial Trump administration actions toward those countries. Kushner's family business actively courted foreign investors by leveraging his White House position, with his sister explicitly promoting their connection to the administration at investor meetings in Beijing. The couple used their government positions to expand international business opportunities while having access to classified intelligence and policy decisions. Their financial disclosures revealed ongoing profits from the Trump International Hotel in Washington D.C., the epicenter of influence peddling during the Trump presidency. The nepotism scandal demonstrated Trump's complete inability to separate personal financial interests from presidential duties, turning the White House into a family business operation.

title: DOJ Subpoenas New York Times Reporters and Their Family Members to Unmask Sources
description_short: DOJ Subpoenas New York Times Reporters and Their Family Members to Unmask Sources
description_medium: In July 2026, the Justice Department subpoenaed New York Times reporters and phone carriers for records connected to reporting on security concerns about the Qatar-gifted Air Force One. The requests also reached family members’ phone records. A federal judge criticized prosecutors’ handling of the subpoenas, and the department withdrew them on July 23 while saying its leak investigation would continue.
description_long: In July 2026, the Trump Justice Department issued grand jury subpoenas to at least three New York Times journalists who had reported on security concerns with Trump's Qatar-gifted Air Force One jet, seeking to compel them to testify about their confidential sources — and then issued additional subpoenas to third-party phone carriers for the reporters' phone and text records, extending to spouses of two reporters and the mother of a third, a step legal experts called extraordinarily aggressive and unorthodox. The subpoenas were signed by Jay Clayton, Trump's U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York, and covered call records dating to January 1, 2026 — months before the articles in question were published, suggesting broad fishing for source relationships. The Times moved to quash the subpoenas before U.S. District Judge Arun Subramanian, whose courtroom saw DOJ lawyers acknowledge they had served subpoenas before completing required preliminary investigative steps — an error prosecutors admitted was a consequence of trying to move too quickly. Judge Subramanian criticized the government's sloppy legal work and the DOJ withdrew the subpoenas on July 23, 2026, but then issued a defiant statement vowing the leak investigation remained ongoing. Attorney General Pam Bondi had earlier in 2025 revoked DOJ policies protecting journalists from subpoenas — policies established after abuses under prior administrations — explicitly to enable aggressive pursuit of government leakers.

title: Press Pool Control Seizure - Century-Old Press Freedom Eliminated
description_short: Press Pool Control Seizure - Century-Old Press Freedom Eliminated
description_medium: In 2025, the White House took control of the presidential press pool’s membership, a role the White House Correspondents’ Association had managed since 1914. Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said the administration would decide which outlets could enter limited spaces such as Air Force One and the Oval Office. The first changes rejected the association’s selection and favored Axios, prompting criticism from press-freedom advocates.
description_long: Donald Trump's White House seized control of the presidential press pool from the White House Correspondents' Association, ending over a century of journalistic independence in covering the presidency while implementing a 'threats, revenge, and punishment' strategy against traditional media. Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt announced that 'The White House press team in this administration will decide who gets into the very small and limited spaces such as Air Force One and the Oval Office,' taking authority that the WHCA had managed since 1914. The administration immediately demonstrated its control by rejecting the correspondents' association's designation of HuffPost as print representative and instead selecting Trump-friendly Axios, showing the plan to 'punish traditional journalists who ask tough questions and promote a parallel universe of pro-Trump media outlets.' The White House Correspondents' Association condemned the move as undermining 'the independence of a free press,' while CNN described it as part of a broader 'troubling turning point in the already-tense dynamic between the Trump White House and the press corps.' The seizure came as the Associated Press was fighting to regain access after being barred from White House events, with the administration systematically excluding news organizations that provided critical coverage. The press pool traditionally includes rotating representatives from television networks, radio, and print media to ensure comprehensive presidential coverage, but Trump's control allows him to reward friendly outlets while punishing independent journalism.

title: Trump withholds $2 billion from Harvard over DEI and Palestine
description_short: Trump withholds $2 billion from Harvard over DEI and Palestine
description_medium: In April 2025, the Trump administration froze more than $2 billion in federal grants to Harvard University. Officials connected the action to campus activism and antisemitism, the university’s diversity programs and curriculum, and international student enrollment. Harvard leaders also received a demand to end the university’s diversity, equity, and inclusion programs.
description_long: The Trump administration froze more than $2 billion in federal grants to Harvard University in April 2025. Officials cited several objections, including campus activism, antisemitism, curriculum, diversity programs, and the number of international students. Harvard’s leadership also received a letter demanding that the university end its diversity, equity, and inclusion programs. The freeze put federal research and education support at the center of a dispute between the administration and one of the country’s oldest universities. The grants affected and the conditions attached to the freeze are not identified here. The case became part of a broader conflict over federal authority, campus policy, and how universities address protests and discrimination.

title: Trump: Mike Johnson claims Trump was an FBI informant tasked with taking down Epstein
description_short: Trump: Mike Johnson claims Trump was an FBI informant tasked with taking down Epstein
description_medium: House Speaker Mike Johnson said Donald Trump had been an FBI informant “to try to take this stuff down” while discussing Trump’s relationship with Jeffrey Epstein. Johnson also tried to explain Trump’s description of the Epstein files as a “hoax.” The remark became part of the public dispute over Trump’s relationship with Epstein.
description_long: House Speaker Mike Johnson said Trump had been an FBI informant who tried to help investigators dealing with Jeffrey Epstein. Johnson made the claim amid renewed controversy over Trump’s relationship with Epstein and Trump’s description of the Epstein files as a “hoax.” He also attempted to explain what he believed Trump meant by that description. The claim was a striking public statement from the speaker of the House because it presented Trump as an informant in the matter he had dismissed as a hoax. The remarks drew attention as lawmakers and reporters sought a fuller account of Trump’s relationship with Epstein and the government’s records about the case.

Journalist Judd Legum described the change as causing a crisis in detainee care and linked it to a disinformation campaign. The shift put responsibility for medical costs and continuity of treatment at issue for outside providers working with detained people. The VA’s reimbursement policy changed while ICE continued to hold people who needed care. The account centers on the funding decision and the resulting dispute over treatment, though the specific providers and patients affected are not named.

description_long: Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem announced on December 18 that she had ordered U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services to suspend the diversity visa lottery, which awards up to 50,000 green cards a year. The suspension put current and prospective applicants in uncertainty while the administration reconsidered the program. title: Trump: Elbridge Colby pauses US-Canada defense board in further gift to Putin and Xi
description_short: Trump: Elbridge Colby pauses US-Canada defense board in further gift to Putin and Xi
description_medium: On May 18, Under Secretary of Defense Elbridge Colby announced that the United States was suspending the Permanent Joint Board on Defense, a bilateral forum established with Canada in 1940. The board let senior officials discuss North American defense, including NORAD. The decision interrupted a longstanding channel for consultation.
description_long: Under Secretary of Defense Elbridge Colby announced on May 18 that the United States would suspend the Permanent Joint Board on Defense, a U.S.-Canada forum established in 1940. The board gave senior officials a regular place to discuss North American defense, including issues involving the North American Aerospace Defense Command. Its suspension interrupted a longstanding consultation channel between the two governments. U.S. and Canadian defense planning includes shared continental responsibilities, but the practical effect of the pause is not documented here. The title’s claim that the decision benefited Russia and China is an interpretation, not a consequence established by the announcement.

title: Trump: CNP List: Over 1,000 Past & Present Members of the Council for National Policy

description_long: The Council for National Policy is the subject of a list naming more than 1,000 past and present members. The entry points to conservative figures Charlie Kirk and Kellyanne Conway and contrasts real political networks with “Deep State” theories circulated by some QAnon followers. A historical report describes conservatives gathering under the council’s umbrella. These details place the organization within conservative political circles, but the list alone does not show what its members did together or how much influence the council exercised. Evidence about its activities and leadership is needed to assess claims about a coordinated network. The connection to Trump also requires more than the presence of conservative figures among its members.

title: Trump: The Tea Party, funded by Koch brothers, aims to take over the Republican party
description_short: Trump: The Tea Party, funded by Koch brothers, aims to take over the Republican party
description_medium: The Tea Party emerged in early 2009 amid public anger over the financial crisis and Barack Obama’s election. About 1,000 people reportedly gathered in St. Louis and described their movement as opposing big government, taxes, and the national debt. The entry links the movement to the Koch brothers and Republican Party politics.
description_long: In February 2009, roughly 1,000 people gathered in St. Louis to protest the financial crisis and Barack Obama’s election. They called themselves the Tea Party and emphasized opposition to big government, taxes, and the national debt. The entry connects the movement to funding from the Koch brothers and describes an effort to reshape the Republican Party. That connection matters because the movement presented itself as grassroots while becoming a force within a major political party. The account does not detail the funding network or the organizations involved, so the extent of outside influence remains unclear.

title: Trump: CNN boss Jeff Zucker tells Michael Cohen he wants Trump to join the network
description_short: Trump: CNN boss Jeff Zucker tells Michael Cohen he wants Trump to join the network
description_medium: CNN president Jeff Zucker called Michael Cohen during the 2016 Republican primary and discussed offering Trump a weekly television show if he lost the nomination. Zucker also gave Cohen debate advice for Trump and called him “the boss.” The conversation raised questions about how CNN’s leadership viewed Trump as a candidate and media figure.
description_long: CNN president Jeff Zucker called Michael Cohen during the 2016 Republican primary and said he would like to offer Donald Trump a weekly television show if Trump lost the nomination. Zucker also discussed debate strategy and referred to Trump as “the boss.” Cohen, then Trump’s lawyer, later described the call. The conversation connected a major news network’s president with a candidate’s inner circle while CNN was covering the campaign. It raises questions about the relationship between CNN and Trump, but does not establish that a formal offer was made or that the network changed its coverage in response. The full call and its date would clarify what Zucker proposed and whether anything followed.
